correctness.rationale: CHECK.py was executed from the actual candidate package. It enumerates exactly 243270 augmented faces and 1843680 Hasse covers, constructs 121536 disjoint elementary matching pairs, finds exactly 198 critical 3-cells, and exhaustively topologically sorts the entire directed Hasse graph, proving acyclicity. Removing the matched empty face leaves one 0-cell and 198 3-cells; finite discrete Morse theory yields an integral wedge of 198 three-spheres. The independent coordinate-line nerve argument yields 57 circles at scale one. The finite Hamming metric has no other critical radii.

originality.rationale: The full relevant primary results prove two complete factors or a three-factor product with one binary factor, and the same papers present the all-nonbinary three-factor case as a conjectural extension. An exact acyclic matching for 3×4×4 is not implied by either theorem or the distinct prior 3×3×3 and 3×3×4 cases. Searches of direct forms, equivalent Hamming notation, numeric tables, and stronger parameter ranges revealed no covering result; residual indexing risk remains.
residual_risks: An unpublished or non-indexed earlier computation might have solved exactly this parameter triple.
Later path-product full text was not inspected beyond abstract; its described scope does not suggest an equivalent theorem.
A statement of the general conjecture or exact Euler count alone would not prove the integral homotopy claim.

value.rationale: The (3,4,4) box is the first natural triple complete-graph product with two four-symbol coordinates in the previously conjectural all-nonbinary regime. It is not the same operation as the already studied binary-factor case or the earlier (3,3,4) box. The proof determines the integral homotopy, absence of torsion and complete barcode, not merely an Euler characteristic. The 198-sphere instance is a reusable exact benchmark for the general published conjecture without claiming to settle it.
